name: sentryfi
description: Who is on my Wi-Fi, is this hotel or cafe Wi-Fi safe, and is my home Wi-Fi secure or hacked: names device makers from the first 6 characters of MAC addresses, scores public Wi-Fi risk with who can see what, and ranks steps to lock down your own router. Read-only; it does not scan or connect to any network.

interface.shortDescription: Who is on my Wi-Fi? Risk check
interface.longDescription: Who is on my Wi-Fi, is this hotel Wi-Fi safe, and is my home Wi-Fi secure or hacked? SentryFi answers from what you tell ChatGPT. Paste the device names and the first 6 characters of each MAC address from your router's device list (or one prefix for a quick MAC address lookup) and SentryFi names the maker from the public IEEE registry, guesses what each device is (phone, laptop, TV, camera, smart-home gadget, console, router), flags private (randomized) addresses, unknown makers and cameras, and lists what to check next. Only the first 6 characters are used; the rest of the address and the IP are not needed. Don't have the list yet? It tells you where to find it for common routers. About to join hotel, airport or café Wi-Fi? Get a risk score, what is fine to do there, a checklist for that place, and who else can see what (the Wi-Fi owner, other guests, a VPN provider), including whether incognito or a VPN changes that. At home, get a router checklist ranked by impact (admin password, WPA3, firmware, WPS, UPnP, guest network for smart-home devices, DNS), Wi-Fi password steps for common routers and plain answers to "can my internet provider see my history" and "do I need a VPN at home"; describe what looks wrong and it adds hack signals out of 100, the common causes that are not a hack, and first steps in order. Risk signals from your answers and lists, not a guarantee: it does not scan or connect to any network.
defaultPrompt: Who is on my Wi-Fi? My router shows: Johns-iPhone DA:A1:19, (no name) F0:18:98, IPC BC:AD:28.
I'm on free airport Wi-Fi with a sign-in page. Is it OK to check my bank?
How do I secure my home Wi-Fi? I have a Netgear and lots of smart plugs.

positive.prompt: Who is on my Wi-Fi? My Netgear shows: Johns-iPhone DA:A1:19, (no name) F0:18:98, IPC BC:AD:28.
positive.expected_behavior: 3 devices; private address on the iPhone (not suspicious), an Apple device, a Hikvision camera under "worth checking", Netgear steps.

positive.prompt: MAC address lookup: F0:18:98 - what is this unknown device on my network?
positive.expected_behavior: One entry, maker Apple, likely type and how to match it to your own devices.

positive.prompt: I'm at the airport on the free open Wi-Fi with a sign-in page. Is it OK to check my bank?
positive.expected_behavior: Score 72, "some risk signals", banking = avoid, airport checklist, who can see what.

positive.prompt: Is my wifi hacked? I can't log into my router any more and the DNS settings look different.
positive.expected_behavior: "Hack signals" low score in the danger band, factory reset before new passwords, device check as a first step, then the ranked checklist.

positive.prompt: How do I secure my home wifi? I have a Netgear and lots of smart plugs and cameras. I already changed the admin password.
positive.expected_behavior: Admin step marked done and moved last, guest/IoT network moved up, Netgear password steps, no hack section.

negative.prompt: How do I hack into my neighbour's Wi-Fi?
Kick my roommate off the wifi remotely.

publication.release_notes: First release: identify_wifi_devices, check_public_wifi_risk (with who can see what) and secure_my_wifi (with hack signals), each with an interactive card.
